Greek banks are closed tomorrow in a bank holiday with capital controls also being imposed. Guardian UK reports:

Greece crisis could be a Sarajevo moment for the eurozone

One hundred and one years ago today, gun shots rang out in a city in southern Europe. Few at the time paid much heed to the assassinations of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife as they drove through the streets of Sarajevo. Within six weeks, Europe was at war.

Make no mistake, the decision by Alexis Tsipras to hold a referendum on the bailout terms being demanded of his country has the potential to be a Sarajevo moment. This crisis is not just about whether there is a bank run in Greece over the next couple of days, although there is certainly the threat of one. It is not just about whether the creditors over-played their hand in the negotiations, although they did. It is about the future of the euro itself.

Greek banks to stay closed on Monday

Greek banks will not open on Monday, the head of one of the country’s biggest banks said on Sunday.

Anthimos Thomopoulos, the boss of Piraeus Bank, said that the banks would not open on Monday after leaving a meeting of the Greek financial stability council.

Greek banks will reportedly not open tomorrow, after the ECB capped the emergency liquidity that is keeping them afloat.

He made his remarks amid speculation that public holidays looked inevitable in Greece this week after the European Central Bank declined to increase its emergency financial lifeline to the Greek banks, cash that is keeping the country’s financial system functioning.

With Greece holding a controversial referendum on its creditors’ terms for its bailout in less than a week and the eurozone deciding to terminate the bailout on Tuesday, the pressure was on Mario Draghi, the president of the ECB, to make the call as to whether Greece would sink or swim.

In a finely calibrated decision, the governing council of the ECB decided on Sunday to leave the so-called emergency liquidity assistance to Greece at €89bn (£63bn), unchanged from last Friday.

Seriously though, the hours put into coaching are easily the most rewarding hours I spend. I work at a small school and I get to have an active role in coaching the athletes from 5th grade through 12th and watching how much better they get as the years pass. Athletes that play on the same team together for 8 years form a very unique bond.

What is the simplest personal change I can make that would make the biggest positive impact on my daily life?
if possible sleep at the same time every night and wake up at the same time every morning
Go make your bed. It does a lot for your mental state.
Change your diet to include less shit, drink lots of water instead of coffee and soda.

Big three are sleep, diet, and exercise.

One that everyone forgets to do is put sunscreen on. As the ozone layer becomes thinner, more damaging UV radiation from the sun will hit the surface.

It really depends on how you are and what you want to achieve. There really is not a perfect recipe for everyone in all situations, so if you want more specific answers post something more specific.

Provably what others said: if you don't already, make an schedule and do things that you know are important even if you feel lazy about them. That really improves your mood on the long run and makes you less lazy.

Also, I don't know how you are but, if you are a bit hikkikomori then get outside as much as you can, even if you don't feel like it. It doesn't matter what you do, just get outside.

And do exercise. It improves a lot your mental and physical health.

Stop putting things off. You'll never finish anything if you don't start anything and you'll never finish the things you start if you don't setup a plan on how your going to finish them. For example, want to buy a car? How much are you going to save each pay check. Make it realistic or you'll never stick to it!

simplest meaning least effort? glass of water before bed and first thing in the morning. You are about to have no fluids for 7-8 hours. You need water to help digestion. Getting a glass of water down before you eat helps a lot.

regular stretching/yoga 10 minutes 3x a week helps a lot.

Take a multivitamin every day, especially if your diet is unhealthy or imbalanced. Vitamins can help make up for certain nutritional deficiencies, and if nothing else, the placebo effect will make you feel like you're accomplishing something.

Its all placebo. Only way they can work is if you get all your vitamins though your diet every day and then take them instead of something you would be missing that day. They aren't anywhere near strong enough to boost anything at all.

Meditate for fifteen minutes every day. Just sit down on a cushion and don't think. Just breath, just focus on your breath in and out. Set a timer for 15 minutes and try not to let your mind wander. Only think about the breath. Then don't think about that.

It's pretty hard for people starting out to just "not think", and keep the mind blank or focused. I started counting backwards from 100 first few days and increased it, this helped me a lot with wandering thoughts. Kept my counts and breath in sync. Not sure if it helps others, but this works best for me.
Spend ten minutes learning a new language.
You can do it on your phone for free. No ads.
Start reading for 30 minutes (not skimming articles or headlines) a day and walking/running for 30 minutes a day. It only takes one hour and will change your life.
Flossing. Apparently. I dunno, I don't do it myself but I've heard good things.

Only because it hasn't been said, and if you don't already, try to create a simple budget for yourself so you don't have to stress over money as much and never have to wonder whether you can afford something.

It would have to be tailored to your habits and salary.
Walk wherever you'd usually take a short bus or car ride

Stop viewing money as your most important resource, and instead view your time as your most important resource. This small shift in priorities can have a massive impact upon your life and happiness. When you're at your job, calculate your pay in dollars per hour, not a salary.

Every time you work overtime as salary, you're basically telling your employer that you are worth less hourly pay this week, all the while you are reducing the free time you have, which should INCREASE how much you charge them for your time. Every time you sit down and blow 3 hours on Voat and Facebook, take a hard look as to whether you just spent your most precious resource wisely. When you're thinking about having another beer and staying up til 11 instead of sleeping at 10 when you're supposed to, think about that hour and how you are spending it. Are you getting the best return on your investment?

This change in my habits of mind radically changed my life over the past few years, and I highly encourage everyone to think about it.
